title: A. The Fair Nut and the Best Path

legend: The Fair Nut is going to travel to the Tree Country, in which there are n$$$n$$$ cities. Most of the land of this country is covered by forest. Furthermore, the local road system forms a tree (connected graph without cycles). Nut wants to rent a car in the city u$$$u$$$ and go by a simple path to city v$$$v$$$. He hasn't determined the path, so it's time to do it. Note that chosen path can consist of only one vertex.

A filling station is located in every city. Because of strange law, Nut can buy only wi$$$w_i$$$ liters of gasoline in the i$$$i$$$-th city. We can assume, that he has infinite money. Each road has a length, and as soon as Nut drives through this road, the amount of gasoline decreases by length. Of course, Nut can't choose a path, which consists of roads, where he runs out of gasoline. He can buy gasoline in every visited city, even in the first and the last.
He also wants to find the maximum amount of gasoline that he can have at the end of the path. Help him: count it.
input: The first line contains a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤3⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of cities.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers w1,w2,…,wn$$$w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_n$$$ (0≤wi≤109$$$0 \leq w_{i} \leq 10^9$$$) — the maximum amounts of liters of gasoline that Nut can buy in cities.

Each of the next n−1$$$n - 1$$$ lines describes road and contains three integers u$$$u$$$, v$$$v$$$, c$$$c$$$ (1≤u,v≤n$$$1 \leq u, v \leq n$$$, 1≤c≤109$$$1 \leq c \leq 10^9$$$, u≠v$$$u \ne v$$$), where u$$$u$$$ and v$$$v$$$ — cities that are connected by this road and c$$$c$$$ — its length.
It is guaranteed that graph of road connectivity is a tree.
output: Print one number — the maximum amount of gasoline that he can have at the end of the path.
note: The optimal way in the first example is 2→1→3$$$2 \to 1 \to 3$$$.
The optimal way in the second example is 2→4$$$2 \to 4$$$.

legend.ai: Nut 将要前往树之国，这个国家有 n$$$n$$$ 个城市。这个国家的大部分土地都被森林覆盖。此外，当地的道路系统构成一棵树(一个无环的连通图)。Nut 想在城市 u$$$u$$$ 租一辆车，并沿一条简单路径前往城市 v$$$v$$$。他还没有确定路径，所以现在需要做出选择。注意，所选路径可以只包含一个顶点。
每个城市都有一个加油站。由于一条奇怪的法律，Nut 在第 i$$$i$$$ 个城市最多只能购买 wi$$$w_i$$$ 升汽油。可以假设他有无限的钱。每条道路都有一个长度，Nut 驾车经过这条道路后，汽油量会减少该道路的长度。当然，Nut 不能选择由一些道路组成的路径，使得他在途中耗尽汽油。他可以在每个到达的城市购买汽油，包括起点和终点城市。
他还想知道在到达路径终点时最多能拥有多少汽油。请帮助他计算这个值。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤3⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$)，表示城市的数量。
第二行包含 n$$$n$$$ 个整数 w1,w2,…,wn$$$w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_n$$$(0≤wi≤109$$$0 \leq w_{i} \leq 10^9$$$)，表示 Nut 在各个城市最多可以购买的汽油量。
接下来的 n−1$$$n - 1$$$ 行中的每一行描述一条道路，包含三个整数 u$$$u$$$、v$$$v$$$、c$$$c$$$(1≤u,v≤n$$$1 \leq u, v \leq n$$$，1≤c≤109$$$1 \leq c \leq 10^9$$$，u≠v$$$u \ne v$$$)，其中 u$$$u$$$ 和 v$$$v$$$ 是由该道路连接的城市，c$$$c$$$ 是道路的长度。
保证道路连通图是一棵树。

output.ai: 输出一个数，表示他在路径终点时最多能拥有的汽油量。

note.ai: 第一个样例中的最优方案是 2→1→3$$$2 \to 1 \to 3$$$。
第二个样例中的最优方案是 2→4$$$2 \to 4$$$。
